## Goal (user story)

As an operator reading the proxy-usage-analysis report, I want the upstream HTTP 429 remediation recommendation to name the mechanism that actually applies, so I do not chase the wrong cooldown when 429s persist.

## Problem statement

The 2026-09-26 proxy-usage-analysis report misattributes every 429 to the `FreeUsageLimitError` 3-hour per-model cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD), even when the observed bodies are `error.type = GoUsageLimitError`. `GoUsageLimitError` bodies take the account-level usage-limit reset quarantine path instead (`_usage_limit_reset_seconds` → `_usage_reset_at`, LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ), which computes a daily/weekly/monthly reset quarantine (30 days + 2 minutes for `metadata.limitName = monthly`). The misleading remediation hides the real recurrence cause (the in-memory quarantine being wiped by proxy restarts; LP-0MUI6KB67005X44B).

## Users

- **Operator / on-call engineer** (primary): reads the generated report to decide whether a persistent 429 is a transient rate limit or an exhausted account quota.
  - *As an operator, when I see GoUsageLimitError 429s, I want the report to point me at the account usage-limit reset quarantine so I can check the account quota rather than wait out a cooldown that is not in effect.*
- **Proxy maintainer** (secondary): uses the recommendation text as the documented behaviour of the routing/quarantine mechanisms.
  - *As a maintainer, I want the report and `SKILL.md` to describe the same mechanism the proxy actually implements, so the docs do not drift from code.*

## Acceptance criteria

1. A fixture 429 body with `error.type = GoUsageLimitError` (and `metadata.limitName = monthly`) produces a recommendation that names the account usage-limit reset quarantine (LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ) and does **not** mention the 3-hour cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD).
2. A fixture 429 body with `error.type = FreeUsageLimitError` still cites the 3-hour cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD).
3. A 429 body with neither recognised error type falls back to the existing generic 429 wording (no fabricated mechanism).
4. Tests cover all three cases; build and full test suite pass.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Repository boundary:** edits are confined to the proxy-usage-analysis skill (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`); implementing requires explicit authorisation via `/skill:implement <id>`.
- **No proxy behaviour change:** this is a reporting/doc correction only; `proxy/proxy/provider.py` routing logic is authoritative and must not change.
- **Parser capability:** the log parser currently extracts only the upstream `error.type` (`RE_UPSTREAM_BODY_TYPE` in `log_parser.py`), not `metadata.limitName` or the reset duration. The recommendation can therefore distinguish by error type only; it cannot literally echo the computed period without a parser change.
- **Backward compatibility:** existing tests asserting the `FreeUsageLimitError` path (e.g. `test_upstream_429_triggers_cooldown_recommendation`) must continue to pass.

## Existing state

- `recommendations.py::_error_recommendations()` builds one recommendation per upstream status bucket; the `status == 429` branch emits a single hard-coded detail naming the 3-hour cooldown regardless of error type.
- The module docstring also states "upstream 429s point at the FreeUsageLimitError cooldown".
- `SKILL.md` (error-analysis bullet list) repeats the same claim: "`upstream error` (HTTP 429) — the 3-hour per-model cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD)...".
- Proxy truth (verified in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`): `_usage_limit_reset_seconds()` is evaluated **before** `_is_free_usage_limit_error()`; it recognises both `GoUsageLimitError` and `FreeUsageLimitError`, parsing "Resets in …" or falling back to `_PERIOD_DEFAULT_SECONDS` (daily=1d, weekly=7d, monthly=30d) plus `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` (120s). Only when no reset can be computed does `_is_free_usage_limit_error()` apply the 10800s `_FREE_USAGE_LIMIT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS`.
- Existing fixture `fixtures.UPSTREAM_429` and tests live in `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`.

## Desired change

Update the 429 recommendation text so the cited mechanism matches the proxy's actual precedence:

- 429 bodies whose bucket contains `GoUsageLimitError` → cite the account-level usage-limit reset quarantine (LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ), noting the quarantine duration is computed from the message's reset time or `metadata.limitName` (daily/weekly/monthly).
- 429 bodies containing `FreeUsageLimitError` (without a reset duration) → cite the 3-hour cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD).
- 429 bodies with neither recognised type → keep the existing generic "check the upstream provider quota or usage limits" wording.
- A bucket mixing both types → describe both mechanisms rather than only one.

Recommended implementation shape: keep one recommendation per status bucket (preserving the current title/severity and the per-status structure) and compose the `detail` from the error types present, so the change is localised and existing per-status tests keep passing. Mirror the corrected wording in the `recommendations.py` docstring and `SKILL.md`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py` — `_error_recommendations()` 429 branch (~line 517) needs per-error-type detail composition; module docstring (~line 419) needs the corrected mechanism description.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/SKILL.md` — the `upstream error` (HTTP 429) bullet (~line 415) must distinguish the two mechanisms.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — add GoUsageLimitError, FreeUsageLimitError, and unrecognised-type cases (near the existing `test_upstream_429_triggers_cooldown_recommendation`, ~line 1371); possibly a mixed-type case.
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — optional `UPSTREAM_429_GO_USAGE_LIMIT` fixture mirroring the observed `GoUsageLimitError` body (log-line parser already extracts the type).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (documented):** AC1 requires naming the quarantine mechanism, not echoing the exact computed period. The parser does not extract `limitName`/reset duration, so the recommendation will name the mechanism and describe how the period is derived, without a literal "30 days". Extending the parser to cite the exact period is out of scope unless the producer requests it.
- **Risk — parser cannot see `limitName` / reset duration.** A `FreeUsageLimitError` that *does* carry a reset duration actually takes the quarantine path in the proxy (because `_usage_limit_reset_seconds` accepts `freeusagelimiterror`), yet the report would cite the 3-hour cooldown based on type alone. This is a residual inaccuracy inherent to the current parser; capture it as a potential follow-up, not scope here.
- **Risk — mixed buckets.** A single 429 bucket can contain several error types; the composition logic must not silently drop the Go path when a Free path is also present.
- **Risk — doc/code drift.** The `SKILL.md` bullet and module docstring must be updated in lockstep with the code to avoid recreating the same misattribution.
- **Scope-creep risk:** the parser enhancement, per-provider/model breakout of 429s, and a live-data regression check are attractive but out of scope; if pursued, record as separate linked work items.

## Related work

- LP-0MUI6KB67005X44B — Persist usage-limit quarantine and provider cooldowns across proxy restarts (open) — the true recurrence cause this report misattribution masks.
- LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ — Recognize GoUsageLimitError and block routing to provider until computed reset time (Daily/Weekly/Monthly) (completed) — the mechanism the Go path must cite.
- LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD — Handle FreeUsageLimitError with 3-hour cooldown on affected model (completed) — the mechanism the Free path must cite.
- LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW — Usage-limit quarantine keyed on endpoint blocks opencode-go and opencode-go-2 together (completed) — account-vs-endpoint quarantine keying.
- LP-0MT652JRM004ZLSI — Remove opencode-big-pickle from proxy provider chains (completed) — retired free-tier provider context.
- LP-0MTLGHFD10015EJG — tangential lint fix surfaced by the automated related-work scan; not a dependency.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What mechanism does a `GoUsageLimitError` 429 actually trigger?** — Answer (agent research): the account-level usage-limit reset quarantine (`_usage_limit_reset_seconds` → `_usage_reset_at`, LP-0MSLJPOCC0001ROJ); `FreeUsageLimitError` without a reset duration triggers the 3-hour cooldown (LP-0MRGU0I91006ODFD). Research: read `proxy/proxy/provider.py` lines 84–103, 3564–3700, 5014–5060; confirmed precedence (reset check before free-limit check). Source: repository inspection.
- **Q: Does the report generator have the upstream `metadata.limitName` / reset duration available?** — Answer (agent research): no. `log_parser.py` captures only `error.type` via `RE_UPSTREAM_BODY_TYPE`; the recommendation must distinguish by error type. Source: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` lines 84–105, 463–470.
- **Q: Rerunning intake (idempotence)?** — The item already contains a goal, observed problem, scope, and ACs; this brief consolidates them and adds the mechanism-precedence evidence, key files, risks, and automatable related work. # `wl delete` of a child reopens an in-progress parent

Discovered while running `/skill:plan LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM` (discovered-from:LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM).

## Problem

Deleting a child work item sets the parent's `status` to `open`, even when the
parent is `in-progress`. This silently breaks the claim invariant
**SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9** ("actively worked => `in_progress`"): an agent that
claims an item, creates/deletes a child, then continues mutating is now
performing work-item mutations while `status: open` — the exact window that
caused the 2026-08-30 duplicate dispatch of `AH-0MTFPDK006QUDC`.

`wl delete <child>` is documented as "marks as deleted", not as touching the
parent, so the parent reversion is unexpected.

## Reproduction (2026-09-26, Worklog via ContextHub)

```bash
# low-priority throwaway parent + child
P=$(wl create --title "__diag_parent__" --stage intake_complete --json | jq -r .workItem.id)
C=$(wl create --title "__diag_child__" --parent "$P" --stage intake_complete --json | jq -r .workItem.id)
wl update "$P" --status in_progress --json >/dev/null
wl show "$P" --json | jq -r .workItem.status   # in-progress
wl delete "$C" --json >/dev/null
wl show "$P" --json | jq -r .workItem.status   # open   <-- unexpected
```

Confirmed on 2026-09-26. `wl update --effort/--risk`, `wl create --parent`,
and `wl dep add` do **not** reproduce it; only child deletion does.

## Expected

Deleting a child must leave the parent's `status`/`stage` untouched (the parent
may legitimately stay `in-progress`; a deleted child does not make the subtree
"finished"). If a reversion is intended for some terminal-parent case, it must
require the parent to be `completed`/`in_review` (as
`demoteParentOnChildAdded` does) and never touch `in-progress`.

## Impact

- Breaks the claim invariant for any skill that deletes children mid-run.
- An item can silently drop out of `wl next`'s in-progress view mid-session.
- Background/downtime dispatchers may re-dispatch an item already being worked.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Reproducing the steps above leaves the parent `in-progress`/`intake_complete`.
- A regression test in the Worklog/ContextHub suite covers child deletion not
  changing a non-terminal parent's status or stage.
- The fix does not reintroduce the terminal-parent demotion behaviour described
  in `demoteParentOnChildAdded` (completed/`in_review` parents still reopen on
  gaining a new child).

## Notes

- Owner/component: Worklog CLI (`ContextHub`) — `wl delete` /
  `packages/shared/src/database.ts`.
- The original `LP-0MU148SHI004WHQM` plan run also showed the parent at
  `open` mid-run without any child deletion; that occurrence is not explained
  by this reproduction and may be a separate sync/concurrency effect, so it is
  not claimed as part of this bug.

## Goal

Persist the provider-availability maps whenever they are mutated, so cooldowns and usage-limit quarantine are durable before the next restart.

## Context

Parent: LP-0MUI6KB67005X44B. Depends on the persistence helpers added in the sibling "Provider-state persistence helpers" child.

Mutation sites to hook:
- `mark_provider_unavailable()` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:1804`) — sets `_provider_unavailable_until[key]`.
- The two usage-limit quarantine assignments: `_usage_reset_at[_reset_account] = time.time() + _reset_seconds` for `GoUsageLimitError` (~line 5022) and `FreeUsageLimitError` (~line 6169).

Writes happen on a cold path (provider failure / upstream 429); a synchronous atomic write is acceptable. A write must never raise into the routing/fallback path. `_provider_failure_count` is explicitly out of scope and must not be persisted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mark_provider_unavailable()` persists the updated cooldown map to the state file.
- Both usage-limit quarantine assignment sites persist the updated `usage_reset_at` map.
- A persistence failure (unwritable directory, disk error) is logged and never raises into the routing/fallback path.
- After each mutation, reloading the state file yields the new key with its absolute expiry (round-trip test per mutation site).
- Expired entries are excluded from the written payload on the next save (no unbounded growth of stale keys).
- `_provider_failure_count` and other in-memory state (sibling-failure counters, local-400 streaks) remain unpersisted.

## Minimal Implementation

- Call `save_provider_state()` at the end of `mark_provider_unavailable()`.
- Call `save_provider_state()` after each `_usage_reset_at[...] = ...` assignment.
- Wrap save calls in a best-effort helper that logs exceptions and swallows them.
- Add mutation round-trip tests.

## Dependencies

- LP-0MUI6KB67005X44B/provider-state-persistence-helpers (persistence helpers).

## Deliverables

- Save hooks in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- Mutation round-trip and save-failure tests.
